newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern launches $3.65 bln debt.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern launches $3.65 bln debt.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp on Tuesday launched a total of $3.65 billion of debt in seven tranches, according to co-lead manager J.P. Morgan Securities.
The deal, initially billed as a $3.0 billion four-tranche offering, was restructured to include tranches of three, 20- and 100-year debt, the manager said.
Tranches launched with official price talk are:
--$400 million three-year debt at 35 to 37 basis points
--$500 million five-year debt at 44 to 46 basis points
--$650 million 40-year debt with a seven-year put option
--$750 million 10-year debt at 65 to 68 basis points over.
--$450 million 20-year debt at 75 to 78 basis points over.
--$650 million 30-year debt at 85 to 88 basis points over.
--$250 million 100-year debt at 95 to 98 basis points

The 20-, 30- and 100-year issues will be priced over the old 30-year Treasury bond and have make-whole calls at Treasuries plus 20 basis points, the manager said. The 40 year put-seven debt also has a make-whole call at Treasuries plus 20 basis points, excercisable after the put date.
The deal is expected to price on Wednesday, according to market sources. Merrill Lynch & Co is also co-lead manager.
